text:
customer-ACME: Hey team — since yesterday ~50% of our requests are hitting eu-west and latency jumped from ~250ms to ~1.2s. We explicitly set ?region=us on our calls. Sample curl we used: ```curl -v 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?region=us' -H 'Authorization: Bearer x...'
X-Client-ID: acme-123
'``` Any idea why router sends us to eu?

alex: Sorry about that — can you paste a full raw request (headers) and a request id from one of the slow traces? Also tell us if you're behind a proxy/nginx or using one of our SDKs.

customer-ACME: Thanks. We're behind our nginx sidecar. Request id: xreq-12345. Raw headers from the proxy (copied): ```
GET /v1/generate?region=us HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer x...
X-Client-ID: acme-123
X-Client-Region: ,us
User-Agent: acme-service/1.2.0
``` Note the X-Client-Region header shows a leading comma — nginx is combining multiple headers from the client and upstream. We haven't modified it intentionally.

support-bot: Created incident INC-7893 and assigned to eng-runtime. Linked traces: https://internal.traces/trace/xreq-12345 :warning:

alex: I can repro the routing behavior in logs — router picked an empty region entry and fell back to our EU default. That's why ?region=us didn't win. Escalating to eng-runtime for precedence bug.

maya: Root cause analysis: our router currently does something like: ```
// pseudo
val = headers['x-client-region'] || params['region']
if val contains ',' then region = val.split(',')[0].trim()
``` The problem: some proxies concatenate repeated/same-name headers into a comma-separated string, and if the concatenation produces a leading comma (",us") split(',')[0] == "" so we treat it as a non-empty header and never check the query param. Edge-case: the header exists but first element is empty -> we treat empty string as a chosen value and fallback to default region (which is eu).

maya: Quick fix (patch) suggestion for router: when splitting header values, filter out empty/whitespace entries and prefer last non-empty value OR fall back to params. Example change: ```
vals = headers['x-client-region'].split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)
if (vals.length) region = vals[vals.length - 1] // prefer last explicit value
else region = params['region']
``` This preserves current behavior for normal headers but ignores accidental leading empties.

ryan: As a short-term mitigation, you can add an nginx rule to normalize the header and drop empty segments. Example snippet to set the header to only non-empty tokens from a single client-supplied header: ```
# in nginx conf
proxy_set_header X-Client-Region "$http_x_client_region";
# or use lua to normalize: if $http_x_client_region ~ "," then rewrite removing empty entries
``` If you want we can apply a hosted-side rewrite to strip leading commas for your org until the router patch lands.

customer-ACME: We'll try patching nginx to trim the header and report back. Appreciate the clear triage and the temporary hosted fix offer — can you enable it for acme-123 if we hit trouble?

alex: Yep — if you can't ship the nginx change quickly, reply here and we'll enable a request-header cleanup for acme-123 (temporary). Also marking INC-7893 as high-priority for a permanent runtime fix. :thumbsup:
